title: Equipment Warranty Terms for Insulin Pump Program Pumps
content:
**1. Malfunction reports.** A pump on an Insulin Pump Program that alarms, fails a self-test or stops delivering insulin is first logged as a manufacturer warranty claim request and troubleshot with the manufacturer's technical support; Larkfield never ships a pump of its own stock to replace a malfunctioning one.

**2. Warranty exchange.** While the pump is in warranty — no later than the manufacturer limited warranty for its model in calendar months after the delivery date of the pump originally supplied on the program, counted in calendar months from that delivery date with that date itself allowed — and the manufacturer confirms a malfunction, the replacement pump ships at no charge as a manufacturer warranty exchange, expedited at no charge, recorded against the original pump shipment and drawing no authorized units.

**3. Remaining warranty.** The replacement carries only the remainder of the original warranty, so the warranty and the payer replacement interval keep counting from the original delivery date.

**4. Return of the malfunctioning pump.** The malfunctioning pump must be sent back in the prepaid box no later than the defective pump return window in calendar days after the replacement's delivery date; when it is received its return is recorded against the exchange shipment, and a pump not received in time is invoiced to the customer by its manufacturer, not by Larkfield.

**5. After the warranty.** A malfunction after the warranty is not a warranty exchange: a new pump is supplied only under the quantity rules for a new pump, and until then the customer is told to use the backup insulin pens or syringes their prescriber ordered.

**6. Loss, theft and accidents.** A pump lost, stolen or damaged by accident is not covered by the manufacturer warranty and is not replaced by Larkfield at no charge.

| Hypothetical case (48-month warranty, original pump delivered on the 20th of a month) | Warranty exchange |
|---|---|
| Malfunction confirmed on the 20th of the month 48 months later | In warranty — that date itself is allowed |
| Malfunction confirmed on the 21st of that month | Out of warranty |
| Pump dropped and cracked within the warranty | Not covered — accidental damage |
